label: Tolerance origin-essentialism rival against Euclidean access at the actual world
summary: Omission countermodel, checked by case analysis (ToleranceOriginRival.Control.Certificate): three origin offsets minus/actual/plus with access iff offsets differ by at most one step (reflexive, symmetric, not Euclidean at actual). Individual false exists and is always present at actual and plus; individual true exists at plus only, present at time 1. Reflexivity at actual, presence-to-existence, inert emptiness and the possible contingent-free past (witness plus, times 0<1) hold; EuclideanAt and NecessaryConcreteAt fail at actual (nothing exists at minus). So the restricted premise is not redundant for ActualEuclidean.inertNecessaryConcrete and the tolerance rival survives Arrival A; neither is refuted. Reading question (prose, unverified): if metaphysical possibility is read as the chained closure of tolerable steps, EuclideanAt holds (group 3: universal frame on three offsets) and the arrival is sound, but then the same assignment loses the possible contingent-free past, because the formerly necessary-at-plus individual becomes contingent; the arrival's other premises must be re-warranted under the closure frame. The tolerance theorist answers that the closure is not metaphysical possibility (one step is possible, a chain is not), so F1 and EuclideanAt cannot simply be transferred; the defender answers that 'possibly possible' is possible under any alethic reading (S4 intuition), which the tolerance view denies only at the price of non-transitive possibility. scripts/countermodel.py does not support the theorem (unsupported parameter inst : Preorder T), so the model was written by hand. The rival is also proved to strengthen the stepwise ReflexiveNonEuclidean rival.
blocker: Which accessibility relation is metaphysical possibility (one tolerable step or its chained closure) remains OPEN; under the closure reading, warrant for the possible contingent-free past and presence-to-existence must be re-assessed; the possible-external-cause arrival (externalNecessaryConcrete) was not tested against the tolerance frame.
